sections.html:
Stratford is a town in Fairfield County at the mouth of the Housatonic River on Long Island Sound. It is part of the Greater Bridgeport Planning Region, with Bridgeport on the west, Trumbull and Shelton to the north and Milford across the river to the east.

The 2020 census counted 52,355 residents. The town covers 19.9 square miles, of which 2.3 are water, and its elevation runs from zero feet along the coast to 295 feet near the northern border.

Stratford was settled in 1639 and named in 1643 for Stratford-upon-Avon in England. It operates under a mayor-council government that began in 2005, with a ten-member council elected by district.

sections.h2: What are the neighborhoods of Stratford?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists more than twenty named neighborhoods, so the street you live on says a lot about the kind of house you own. Here are some of them:

  • Lordship, Long Beach and Short Beach on the shoreline.
  • Paradise Green, a shopping and park area with a pharmacy, restaurants and a bakery.
  • Stratford Center and the Historic District around the oldest settlement.
  • Putney, home to the 30-acre Boothe Memorial Park.
  • Oronoque, Oronoque Hills and Oronoque Village in the north.
  • Success Village, Beaver Dam, Birdseye, Hollister Heights, Peck's Mill, Stony Brook Gardens and the South End.

Shore parcels near Long Beach and Short Beach are on the Sound, and the Housatonic River borders the town on the east. A buyer will ask about flood zone and flood insurance, so have that answer ready.

Aircraft manufacturing is the backbone of the local economy. Sikorsky Aircraft, a Lockheed Martin subsidiary, has its headquarters here and is by far the largest employer.

Igor Sikorsky flew an early commercial helicopter at his Stratford plant in 1939, and every Marine One helicopter has been built in town since 1957. Because so many households depend on one large employer, a contract change at the plant can ripple through local housing decisions.

sections.h2: What about the Raymark and Army Engine Plant sites?
sections.html:
Stratford has two federal environmental cleanup sites: the Raymark Industries site, on the EPA's National Priorities List, and the former Stratford Army Engine Plant, which the U.S. Army is cleaning up outside that list.

Raymark made brake pads and friction products here from 1919 to 1989 and disposed of waste containing lead, asbestos and PCBs, some of which was used as fill. The EPA finished cleaning contaminated residential properties in 1995 and the former plant property in 1997, and plans for the Ferry Creek area were still being developed, according to Wikipedia.

If you own a house in a neighborhood touched by this history, buyers, lenders and attorneys may ask for records. Contact the EPA or the Connecticut environmental agency for parcel-specific information. Any buyer, cash or financed, will want to see the paperwork.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and the airport serve Stratford?
sections.html:
Stratford is served by Interstate 95, U.S. Route 1, the Merritt Parkway (Route 15) and state Routes 108, 110, 113 and 130. Sikorsky Memorial Airport is inside the town, though the City of Bridgeport owns it.

The Metro-North station is on the New Haven Line, 59 miles from Grand Central Terminal, and the ride into Manhattan takes about 90 minutes. The station has limited parking, fewer than 300 spaces, and a bus connection to Bridgeport.

Airport noise and flight paths are a known consideration for houses near the field, so a seller near it should be ready for that question. Houses near I-95 or Route 1 also draw questions about road noise.

sections.h2: How did Stratford's history shape its housing?
sections.html:
Stratford grew in two big surges. The census count was 12,347 in 1920, 33,428 in 1950 and 45,012 in 1960, alongside the growth of its aircraft and defense plants, and it has stayed between about 49,000 and 52,000 since 1970.

The older core includes the Stratford Center Historic District, Stratford Point Light and several colonial houses on the National Register, such as the Capt. David Judson House. The town also saw the first Anglican church in Connecticut, founded in 1707.

Large local sites have changed too. The Stratford Army Engine Plant closed on September 30, 1998 and its 78 acres were auctioned in 2008, though the winning bid was not paid, and the American Shakespeare Theatre on the Housatonic stood vacant from the mid-1980s until it burned in 2019. Owners of nearby houses have watched those properties for years, so ask the town planning office what is currently proposed.

sections.h2: What do Stratford's schools and town services look like?
sections.html:
The Stratford Board of Education operates 13 schools for about 6,800 students: two high schools (Bunnell and Stratford High), two middle schools (Flood and Wooster) and nine elementary schools. Two Catholic schools, St. James and St. Mark, serve kindergarten through eighth grade.

The town's fire department runs from four stations, and its police department has 98 officers, according to Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What does a Stratford seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
The seller owes Connecticut's conveyance tax: three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town, a total of one percent on a typical house (Chapter 223). A $450,000 sale would owe $4,500.

The statute also sets the state rate at 1.25 percent for non-residential property and for residential prices above $800,000, and 2.25 percent above $2.5 million. Exemptions exist for deeds in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence and for transfers between spouses.

The state's instructions say the seller or the seller's attorney files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and that pay-by-bank-account filing is available in towns on the myCTREC system (DRS). Stratford's town code on that form is 138. The Stratford town clerk can confirm local recording steps.

sections.h2: How and when are Stratford property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Connecticut towns choose between one, two and four installments, as long as the last one falls due at least 45 days before the fiscal year ends (Chapter 204). Stratford's Tax Collector sets the schedule, so ask that office for the due dates and for a payoff figure before closing.

Under state law an installment unpaid by the first of the following month is delinquent, and interest of 18 percent a year runs back to the due date, with a $2 minimum per installment unless the town waives it. The Assessor can explain your assessment and the appeal steps.

sections.h2: Why would a Stratford owner choose a cash sale?
sections.html:
Owners usually choose it for speed, for a condition problem or for a complicated situation like an inherited house, back taxes or a move on a deadline. A cash purchase does not rely on a lender's appraisal, so repairs do not hold up the closing.

We buy houses in Stratford and nearby Fairfield County towns as-is, and we explain how the offer is figured. Compare it with a listing, subtract repairs, carrying costs and the conveyance tax, and decide which route fits.

faqs.q: What county is Stratford, CT in?
faqs.a: Stratford is in Fairfield County, on Long Island Sound at the mouth of the Housatonic River, with a 2020 census population of 52,355.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Stratford?
faqs.a: Lockheed Martin-Sikorsky Aircraft, with 5,734 employees in the town's 2025 financial report, followed by the Town of Stratford with 1,613.

faqs.q: How much conveyance tax will I pay selling a Stratford house?
faqs.a: Most homes owe one percent of the price, 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town. On $450,000 that is $4,500.

faqs.q: Does the Raymark Superfund site affect every house in Stratford?
faqs.a: No. The Raymark and Army Engine Plant sites are specific locations, and the EPA finished cleaning contaminated residential properties in 1995. Ask the EPA about a specific parcel.

faqs.q: How long is the train from Stratford to Grand Central?
faqs.a: About 90 minutes on the New Haven Line, according to Wikipedia.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Stratford house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses in their current condition, and the cost of repairs is reflected in the offer.
